recipes.subject: TagDistribution.per_type/3's tenant opts are read via Keyword.get(opts,:workspace_id) / Keyword.get(opts,:project_id) then piped into scope_to_workspace_or_global/3 — nil,nil resolves to the GLOBAL (all-tenant) read the daily worker deliberately uses; a controller must instead pass BarkparkWeb.ScopeHelpers.scope_opts(conn) (or an equivalent [workspace_id:, project_id:] pair from conn.assigns) so a public tag-browse read is tenant-scoped, not global
recipes.expect: per_type/3 does `workspace_id = Keyword.get(opts, :workspace_id)`; `project_id = Keyword.get(opts, :project_id)` then `|> scope_to_workspace_or_global(workspace_id, project_id)`, with the marker comment directly above the call reading 'D45 tag-count distribution is deliberate instance-wide admin telemetry — the daily TagDistribution worker reads across all tenants (workspace_id nil -> global)'

recipes.subject: docs_with_tag/4 (content/query.ex) already establishes the exact controller-facing pattern per_type/3 must copy: same Keyword.get(opts,:workspace_id)/:project_id) -> scope_to_workspace_or_global/3 idiom, called with a real request's opts
recipes.expect: docs_with_tag/4 reads workspace_id/project_id from opts identically to per_type/3 and pipes scope_to_workspace_or_global(workspace_id, project_id) — title-ordered (asc: d.title, asc: d.doc_id), no strength ORDER BY arm yet

recipes.subject: GET /v1/data/counts/:dataset (#4377, QueryController.counts/2, manifest id data.counts) groups ONLY by d.type — a flat {type=>N} map — and is a structurally different shape from TagDistribution.per_type's {type,tag}=>N; extending it to carry a tag dimension would break its documented FROZEN response shape ('the Go bare-noun slice consumes it verbatim')
recipes.expect: counts/2 docstring: 'FROZEN response shape, which the CLI slice consumes verbatim: {"ok":true,"dataset":..,"perspective":"published","counts":{type=>N}}' — grouped by d.type only, no tag axis anywhere in the query

recipes.subject: the open task pds-bl-counts-perspective-honesty is an ORTHOGONAL axis (perspective published/drafts/raw honesty on the existing /v1/data/counts route) — it neither blocks nor is satisfied by adding a tag dimension; it's a separate fix on the same file
recipes.rerun: bp task get pds-bl-counts-perspective-honesty -o json | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d['doc']['content']['description'][:300])"
recipes.expect: description starts '...GET /v1/data/counts/:dataset accepts a perspective query param and IGNORES it entirely...' — about perspective, not about a tag/type breakdown

recipes.subject: ROOT CAUSE of `bp doc query document` 404ing: NOT a route-segment collision. doc.get/doc.ls/doc.query are manifest auth_tier:"none", so authHeaders() sends NO Authorization header at the default published perspective (run.go:369-375) — confirmed by proxying the real bp process: the /v1/capabilities preflight carried 'Authorization: Bearer ...' but the subsequent GET /v1/data/query/production/document?limit=1 carried NONE, and the server 404s an anonymous read of a type with no public schema (existence-hiding) exactly as it does for `post` (0 docs) while paper/tag/command/metric/task (all public schemas) succeed anonymously
recipes.rerun: python3 tooling_scratch_proxy.py & BARKPARK_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8933 bp doc query document --limit 1 -o json  # proxy logs show the 2nd request has no Authorization header while /v1/capabilities did
recipes.expect: bp doc query document 404s ('document not found') at default perspective; `bp doc query document --perspective drafts` (forces needsPerspectiveAuth=true, run.go:87-125) succeeds and returns the real doc — proving the token, not the route, was the missing ingredient

recipes.subject: doc.backlinks and data.counts are correctly manifest auth_tier:"read" (always attach bearer) — the pattern a NEW tag-browse/tag-detail manifest command must copy so an authenticated bp caller never hits the same silent 404 the wish's MUST-RUN probe surfaced
recipes.rerun: TOKEN=$(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('$HOME/.config/barkpark/config.json'))['token'])"); curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://guerrilla.barkpark.cloud/v1/capabilities | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);[print(c['id'],c['auth_tier']) for c in d['commands'] if c['id'] in ('doc.backlinks','data.counts','doc.query')]"
recipes.expect: doc.backlinks read, data.counts read, doc.query none

recipes.subject: router.ex mounts confirm two distinct client patterns: backlinks/counts/query/doc (dataset-scoped: flat /v1/data/... + preview /v1/preview/... + scoped /w/:workspace_slug/p/:project_slug/... mirrors, pipe_through [:api,:api_grant_read] or :shared_docs_api) vs /v1/graph/* (global: ONE mount under scope "/v1" with pipe_through [:api,:require_token], no workspace/project prefix, dataset rides a ?dataset= query param). Tag-browse/tag-detail reads are per-tenant dataset-scoped counts/doc-lists (TagDistribution.per_type/docs_with_tag both take dataset as a REQUIRED positional arg, matching backlinks/counts) so they should follow the backlinks/counts (dataset-scoped) pattern, not the graph.ts (global) pattern — a shared-vocabulary tag route on the global pattern would leak cross-tenant tag existence/usage, the exact class data_counts_test.exs guards counts against
recipes.expect: backlinks/counts appear 3-4x across /v1/data (flat), /v1/preview, and /w/:workspace_slug/p/:project_slug scopes; graph_show appears once under a bare scope "/v1" with no workspace/project prefix
